@copilot Update this PR directly with all six repository-audit follow-ups below and the additional cached-value JFR registrations. The verified target is open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation, head branch `trask-metric-callback-classloaders`, based on `main`. Preserve the existing changes in this PR. Keep the branch assigned by GitHub Copilot cloud agent; do not rename it or create a replacement branch. If the platform assigns a follow-up branch, keep that assigned branch.

The rule added by this PR distinguishes SDK strong callback captures, the independently saved registering thread context class loader (TCCL), registration ownership, and references retained by closed handles. The repository-wide static audit was performed at 61aa7c4f3a80b3e16d18c82260c968dc978de571, then compared with this PR. Recheck relevant code and supported dependency contracts on the actual PR head before changing it. The bundled SDK 1.68.0 saves the registration TCCL strongly and retains callback/TCCL fields in closed observable handles. Weak callback captures alone do not eliminate that saved-loader path.

1. Fix both ordinary and batch API-bridge registrations in `instrumentation\opentelemetry-api\opentelemetry-api-1.10\javaagent\src\main\java\io\opentelemetry\javaagent\instrumentation\opentelemetryapi\v1_10\metrics\CallbackAnchor.java`, including the callers in the 1.15 batch bridge. `anchor()` and `anchorBatch()` currently invoke `buildFn.apply(weak)` under the original TCCL, so the SDK still pins an application loader despite the bootstrap weak wrappers. Remove that strong SDK loader reference without changing application callbacks to execute under null instead of their expected original loader. Preserve class-loader-local strong anchoring/refcounts for the intended reporting lifetime and bootstrap-safe weak callback delegation. Trace the defining loaders and retained cleanup state, not only weak target fields. Extend the existing classloader-collection coverage to actually set the disposable application loader as registration TCCL and cover ordinary and batch behavior plus callback execution-loader restoration.

2. Fix all nine Micrometer SDK registration calls in `OpenTelemetryGauge`, `OpenTelemetryFunctionCounter`, `OpenTelemetryFunctionTimer`, `OpenTelemetryLongTaskTimer`, and `OpenTelemetryMeter`, beneath `instrumentation\micrometer\micrometer-1.5\library\src\main\java\io\opentelemetry\instrumentation\micrometer\v1_5`. The double/long measurement recorders save the original TCCL weakly, but SDK registration currently saves it strongly. Register without that extra strong SDK reference while preserving the recorders' existing weak-loader execution and restoration behavior. Construct recorders before entering any null-TCCL helper, so they capture the real original loader. Obtain/configure builders and factories before the helper too. Do not blanket-weaken measurement functions or claim arbitrary app-defined functions become collectible while still strongly held.

3. Connect Micrometer registry shutdown to async unregister cleanup. `OpenTelemetryMeterRegistry` currently connects `RemovableMeter.onRemove()` only through `config().onMeterRemoved(...)`. Micrometer's supported baseline 1.5.0 and current `MeterRegistry.close()` call each meter's `close()`, not removal listeners. Wire the supported shutdown path to the same cleanup, preserving other meters' close behavior and idempotent removal/close handling. Hidden-meter mode can make this registry's `getMeters()` return empty, so do not rely on that override to enumerate actual meters for cleanup. Verify callback disappearance after normal registry close, including hidden-meter mode.

4. Release callback-bearing state after closing registrations where the closed owner can remain reachable. In the API bridge, cover all six `ApplicationObservable*` handle wrappers in the 1.10 metrics package and `ApplicationBatchCallback` in the 1.15 metrics package: their final SDK delegate and `onClose` references survive close, and `CallbackAnchor.releaseOnClose()` keeps capturing the original callback even after removing the anchor. Release both handle and callback-bearing cleanup state while preserving one-shot release, refcounts, close semantics, and supported concurrency. In the five Micrometer async implementations above, close and clear stored handles/lists on removal/shutdown. In `instrumentation\runtime-telemetry\library`, clear `RuntimeTelemetry`'s observables collection and the collections closed by `internal\RecordedEventHandler.closeObservables()` after cleanup. Preserve required error handling. Add focused retained-owner coverage proving unrelated registration loaders/callback state can be collected after close. Do not incorrectly expect an owner to release its own defining loader while the owner remains alive. Hikari's equivalent fix is already in this PR.

5. Give custom Micrometer meter measurements a strong lifetime owner. `OpenTelemetryMeter` creates `DoubleMeasurementRecorder<>(measurement, Measurement::getValue, attributes)` but only retains observable handles; the recorder holds each `Measurement` weakly and `measure()` returns empty. Once the builder/input iterable is discarded, measurements can be collected while the meter is still registered, stopping reporting. Baseline Micrometer `DefaultMeter` strongly stores the supplied measurements. Retain the internal `Measurement` wrappers for this custom meter's reporting lifetime and release them at removal/shutdown. Do not strengthen ordinary gauge targets as a blanket fix. Cover continued custom-meter reporting after discarding construction inputs and forcing GC, plus cleanup.

6. Fix Dropwizard per-registry registration ownership in `instrumentation\dropwizard\dropwizard-metrics-4.0\javaagent\src\main\java\io\opentelemetry\javaagent\instrumentation\dropwizardmetrics\v4_0`. `MetricRegistryInstrumentation` adds the same `DropwizardSingletons.metrics()` listener to every registry, while `DropwizardMetricsAdapter.otelGauges` indexes handles only by metric name. Two registries may both contain gauge `x`: adding B overwrites A's handle, removing A closes B's handle, and removing B leaves A's callback registered forever. Give registrations real per-registry ownership so coexistence and removals clean up the correct callbacks without stopping the other registry's valid metric. Simply closing the overwritten callback is not sufficient. Preserve supported metric behavior and verify two registries with the same gauge name, removal in both orders, and no remaining callback after both removals.

Also apply the existing `MetricCallbackRegistration.withoutContextClassLoader(...)` helper to the other 21 cached-value registrations in these nine JFR handlers beneath `instrumentation\runtime-telemetry\library\src\main\java17\io\opentelemetry\instrumentation\runtimetelemetry\internal`: `buffer\DirectBufferStatisticsHandler`, `classes\ClassesLoadedHandler`, `container\ContainerConfigurationHandler`, `cpu\OverallCpuLoadHandler`, `memory\CodeCacheConfigurationHandler`, `memory\G1HeapSummaryHandler`, `memory\MetaspaceSummaryHandler`, `memory\ParallelHeapSummaryHandler`, and `threads\ThreadCountHandler`. Their callbacks read cached primitive values and fixed attributes. Verify that property in current code. Keep all builder/factory lookup and configuration outside the helper, as the existing `ContextSwitchRateHandler` change does. Preserve telemetry names, values, units, attributes, and close lifecycle.

Acceptance requires all six follow-ups and all nine additional JFR handlers, with focused regression tests for changed ownership, shutdown, GC, and TCCL behavior. Read CONTRIBUTING.md and applicable topic instructions; reuse existing helpers/GC test facilities and preserve compatibility with supported dependency versions. Run the narrowest applicable `spotlessApply` directly before targeted validation, never `spotlessCheck` as a preliminary step. Run relevant focused tests where feasible and report exact outcomes or blockers. Do not blanket-null TCCL for provider-backed JMX/MXBean, OSHI, shared pool, Kafka, or arbitrary application functions. No unrelated cleanup, additional PRs/tasks, merges, or changes outside this assignment.

+## Observable metric callbacks
+
+The SDK bundled with the javaagent holds the callback strongly. Separately, it saves the
+registering thread's context class loader (TCCL) and uses it to run the callback. Registering
+with a null TCCL does not weaken what the callback holds. Weak references in the callback do
+not remove the SDK's saved TCCL.

+**Registration ownership.** Identify who owns the registration and when it ends. Verify that
+every supported shutdown or replacement path reaches the instrumentation's cleanup. Close
+the returned handle and remove any long-lived registry entries for that registration.
+Clearing a reference to the handle without closing it does not unregister the callback.
+
+After `close()`, the SDK handle still holds the callback and the saved TCCL. If either
+should be collectible while the owner is still alive, clear the field that stores the
+closed handle, for example by setting it to `null`.
+
+A callback can strongly hold state that should live as long as the registration. For example,
